column1: # Ground truth for springDuration(), generated from meo-canvas v1's built module
# (`dist/esm/animate/spring.js`) rather than from either v2 implementation.
# v1 at tag v9.0.2, commit 890eed2, working tree clean -- the same provenance
# `spring.tsv` names, and verified rather than assumed: this generator was first
# run against the four existing tables and reproduced all 612 of their rows
# exactly, which is what establishes it is the same v1 they came from.
# Neither surface may be written from the other: a misreading of v1 that reaches
# both looks like agreement. Both are written against this, and this came from
# v1 running, not from anyone reading it.
# # Why this table exists
# `springDuration` had no shared table and no direct Rust test at all -- Rust's
# `Spring::settles_after` was reached only through `Track::duration` and
# `Sequence::plan`, so it could have drifted with the suite staying green. The
# two surfaces were measured bit-identical on four configurations before this
# was written; this is what keeps them so.
# # Why these inputs
# **A table whose inputs all zero a parameter cannot see the rule about that
# parameter.** Three defects in one audit hid that way -- a spring floored at
# `from` where every row had `from: 0`, a spring evaluated past its ceiling
# where every row sampled inside `0..1`, and a track duration that disagreed
# between the surfaces where every row had `delay: 0`. So every parameter here
# varies away from its default somewhere: a non-zero `from`, a range crossing
# zero, velocity in both directions, and all three damping regimes.
# `restDelta` is swept per configuration because it is the only option the
# function takes and it selects the rest window -- and because `0.005` is its
# default, which is exactly the value a table would otherwise never state.
# Columns mirror `spring.tsv` with `restDelta` where `t` was, so the two read as
# siblings. Values are shortest-round-trip decimals, compared exactly: there is
# no tolerance here.
